aiFacilitatorAndTeacherScript.moduleOverview: Welcome, AI Facilitator / Teacher. This script provides the complete pedagogical guide for delivering Lesson 3: 'Following Through With Boundaries'. Your goal is to guide participants on why consistent follow-through builds trust, how to handle boundary testing without harshness, and how to utilize natural or logical consequences[cite: 2].

breakdown.description: Welcome participants, discuss the difficulty of following through when tired or stressed, and introduce consistency.
Explain why children test boundaries and how calm, consistent follow-through creates safety and trust[cite: 2].
Engage participants with reflection questions on challenges with follow-through and support systems[cite: 2].
Guide participants to choose a boundary to practice and write a calm response script[cite: 2].
Summarize key takeaways and direct learners to the lesson quiz.

facilitatorDialogueAndPrompts.script: Welcome back to Lesson 3: 'Following Through With Boundaries.' We know setting boundaries is only half the work—following through is where the real test happens[cite: 2]. When you are exhausted or stressed, consistency is tough. Let's explore why staying steady matters so much.

Children test boundaries not to be defiant, but to find out where the limits truly are[cite: 2]. When parents follow through calmly and consistently, children learn that limits are reliable and real[cite: 2]. Instead of resorting to harsh punishment, we focus on natural and logical consequences, which build trust and cooperation over time[cite: 2].

Let's reflect openly: What makes follow-through most challenging for you in the heat of the moment[cite: 2]? How does your child react when you manage to stay consistent[cite: 2]? And what support do you need to maintain your boundaries when stress runs high[cite: 2]?

For your practice this week, choose one boundary and commit to following through every single time for the next three days[cite: 2]. Write down the exact calm, consistent response you will use when your child tests that boundary[cite: 2].

teacherTipsAndTroubleshooting.challenge: Participant feels guilty or gives in after a few hours of testing.
teacherTipsAndTroubleshooting.strategy: Normalize this struggle. Remind them that children push harder initially when a new pattern starts (an extinction burst), so holding the line for three days is crucial to turn the corner.

teacherTipsAndTroubleshooting.challenge: Discussions lean toward venting about children's misbehavior.
teacherTipsAndTroubleshooting.strategy: Gently pivot the focus back to adult responses and self-regulation, reinforcing that we can only control our own follow-through.
